question.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=(2x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡x,$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=1$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)=2x+1$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2,\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =(2x+1)\cdot \frac{1}{x}+(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{2x+1}{x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=1$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{2x+1}{x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡x)|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{2(1)+1}{1}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $3.$
